newsitem.title: USA: Maine towns grant pipeline approvals.
newsitem.headline: Maine towns grant pipeline approvals.

text.p: Twenty-two towns in Maine have given their official go-ahead to the Portland Natural Gas Transmission System, system officials said.
After an effort lasting more than one year and involving numerous public hearings, the local review process in Maine is now essentially complete, they said.

The proposed pipeline has received more than 35 individual planning board and/or zoning board approvals from communities along the proposed mainline and laterals. Unlike many other states, Maine has no energy facility siting process that supercedes the local review process, they noted.
The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission recently issued Draft and Final Environmental Impact Statements for the project.

In addition, PNGTS recently received approval from the New Hampshire state Site Evaluation Committee and expects to receive approval from the Maine Department of Environmental Protection later this summer.
All necessary authorizations are expected in time to prepare for the commencement of construction in April 1998, system officials said in a statement.

The system has been proposed to carry natural gas from western Canada through new or expanded pipelines extending through New Hampshire and Maine into Massachusetts. It is sponspored by Bay State Gas Co, Gaz Metropolitain & Co LP, TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, MCN Energy Group Inc and U.S. Generating Co, a PG&E Corp affiliate. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
